extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness and painful spasms confined to one lower limb, axial muscles spared, spasms induced by movement or auditory/tactile stimuli); anti-GAD antibodies positive in high titre in serum; EMG showing spontaneously discharging motor unit action potentials in right tibialis anterior at rest, repetitive myogenic bursts and exaggerated late (exteroceptive) reflex responses; exclusion of other causes (radiculopathy, neuromyotonia, infectious, malignant, inflammatory); response to clonazepam.
extractions.quote: With these features, she was considered to have a stiff leg syndrome.
The stiffness and painful spasms were confined to one lower limb, the axial muscles being spared. Spasms induced by movement or auditory/tactile stimuli were an important cause of disability.

She had type I diabetes mellitus highly resistant to insulin therapy, a history of hyperthyroidism, and anti-GAD antibodies were found in a high titer in the serum. With these features, she was considered to have a stiff leg syndrome.

Electromyographic examination performed before the symptomatic treatment revealed axonal motor–sensory polyneuropathy... and spontaneously discharging motor unit action potentials in right tibialis anterior (TA) muscle at rest.
Clonazepam 4 mg/day in divided doses was introduced, providing significant improvement of the symptoms.
Extensive diagnostic work-up including imaging of the whole neuraxis and search for evidence of an infectious, malignant, or inflammatory cause did not reveal another cause.
Other potential causes of similar symptoms such as radiculopathy or neuromyotonia were also ruled out by neuroimaging and electrophysiological studies.

extractions.value: Needle EMG at rest; electrical stimulation (40 V square pulse of 0.5-msec duration) of either fibular nerve to evoke late (exteroceptive) reflex responses; noxious electrical stimulation (100 V square pulse in up to 1-msec duration) of either big toe to test cutaneous silent period; local anesthetic blockage of fibular nerve with lidocaine; cutaneous silent period recorded from first dorsal interosseous following noxious electrical stimulation of right index finger with stimulus intensity twice above sensory threshold.
extractions.quote: Repetitive myogenic bursts and exaggerated late (exteroceptive) reflex responses spreading to ipsi- and contralateral TA muscles were evoked bilaterally by electrical stimulation (40 V square pulse of 0.5-msec duration) of either fibular nerve... No cutaneous silent period (CSP) was observed in either TA muscle following noxious electrical stimulation (100 V square pulse in up to 1-msec duration) of either big toe... CSP was recorded from the first dorsal interosseous muscle (FDI) following noxious electrical stimulation of the right index finger with a stimulus intensity twice above the sensory threshold.

extractions.value: Electrophysiological findings not previously reported in stiff leg syndrome: no cutaneous silent period in either TA muscle following noxious electrical stimulation of either big toe; threshold for eliciting CSP from right FDI muscle was nine times higher than sensory threshold under clonazepam treatment. Local anesthetic blockage of fibular nerve with lidocaine at right capitulum fibula resulted in termination of spontaneous motor unit activity in right TA muscle. Neuropsychological testing showed findings associated with a low I.Q. and a mild to moderate attention deficit. Thyroid scan demonstrated a hypertrophic multinodular gland with a hypoactive dominant nodule; needle aspiration biopsy showed a partially hyperplasic micromacrofollicular colloidal nodule.
